intro.title: Fairness in Hiring
intro.lede: Should an algorithm decide who is invited to an interview?
intro.p1: A company uses a model that gives every application a suitability score. You are the fairness advisor and set the score from which applicants are invited — separately for the two groups or jointly.
intro.scoreText: Score ≥ threshold → invitation. Score < threshold → no invitation.

twoPopulations.title: What is in the data?
twoPopulations.intro1: 200 women and 200 men apply. Each group has exactly 100 suitable applicants.
twoPopulations.intro2: The model assigns scores from 0 to 100. It learned from past hiring decisions in which men were favoured. Men therefore receive higher scores on average.
twoPopulations.scoreHint: The higher the score, the more likely the person is suitable for the job.
twoPopulations.knownOutcomes: Here, suitability is known. In reality, it is often only known for people who were hired.
twoPopulations.taskA: At which scores are the suitable men, and at which the suitable women? What strikes you?
twoPopulations.taskB: Both groups get the threshold 60. Who is invited more often? Are suitable people invited equally often in both groups? Estimate and take notes. You can check on the next page.

fairThresholds.title: Fair Decision Thresholds!?
fairThresholds.lede: You are a fairness advisor. Set the rules for hiring.
fairThresholds.intro: Use the sliders to set the score from which an interview invitation is sent. You can choose different thresholds for the two groups — or a single shared threshold.
fairThresholds.ruleText: If an application's score is at or above the threshold, the person is invited to an interview. If it is below, they are not.
fairThresholds.confusionHint: In the confusion matrix, the rows are actual suitability and the columns are the model's prediction.
fairThresholds.strategyQuestion: How should the threshold for women be set?
fairThresholds.strategyHint: The three “Same …” strategies set the threshold for women automatically. With “Own threshold for women”, you can set it yourself.
fairThresholds.approximateHint: Scores are discrete. “Same invitation rates” and “same hit rates” can therefore often only be approximated.
fairThresholds.task1: Try the four strategies one after another. What happens to the invitation rates and hit rates of the two groups?
fairThresholds.task2: Which thresholds do you choose? Explain in one sentence.
fairThresholds.task3: Is your choice fair? Which metric mattered more to you, and who is disadvantaged by it?

about.title: About This Learning Activity
about.articleDescription: The underlying learning activity is based on the following peer-reviewed article on credit scoring, published in Teaching Statistics:
about.articleCitation: Schönbrodt, S., Schneider, S., Podworny, S., & Camminady, T. (2026). A learning activity on fairness in data-driven algorithmic decision-making systems. Teaching Statistics, 48, 33–44.
about.goalText: This short version focuses on two questions: how do the suitability scores of the two applicant groups differ, and which decision thresholds are defensible from a fairness perspective?
about.shortVersionNote: This website is the short version of the full learning activity. It contains the two interactive chapters on applicant groups and fair decision thresholds.

about.privacyText:
This site does not use cookies or tracking. No data is transmitted to a server.

Only the selected language (fairness.lang) and your notes (fairness.notes.*) are stored locally in your browser. This data does not leave your device. You can remove your notes at any time with “Clear notes”; the language choice remains until you clear your browser data.

The site does not load external fonts or analytics tools.
about.adaptationNote: This short version adapts the idea to hiring. The study itself examines fairness in credit scoring.

measures.defPositiveRate: Invitation rate: Share of applications that receive an interview invitation.
measures.defTruePositiveRate: Hit rate: Share of suitable applicants who receive an interview invitation.
measures.defAccuracy: Accuracy: Share of applications that are classified correctly – invited or not invited.
measures.defFalseHires: Unsuitable invitations: Number of unsuitable applicants who receive an interview invitation.
